summary: A Claude seat on an auto install reads the source tree and scratch without asking a person, and never reads credential paths

replay.detail: No stored history or replay change.

schema.detail: No database, claim or configuration schema change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or coordination version change.

compatibility.detail: Claude's auto mode treats a read in another repository as scope escalation and asks a person ('Read outside the working directories'), so an unattended seat stalled on it and raised a waiting-for-permission alert on a person's home. st's auto-mode Claude launch now adds Read rules to the seat's settings, merged with any authored --settings: allow ~/src, /var/tmp, /private/var/tmp (macOS) and /nix/store, plus, for a workspace under a directory named github.com outside ~/src (such as ~/Developer/github.com on a Mac), that github.com tree strictly inside the home directory; any other layout adds nothing, and deny the credential and login paths (~/.ssh, ~/.config/gh, ~/.config/fabric, ~/.config/sekrets, ~/.sekrets, ~/.claude-accounts, ~/.claude/.credentials.json, ~/.claude.json, ~/.codex/auth.json, ~/.codex/config.toml, ~/.npmrc, st's keys and accounts directories, ~/.config/st3); deny wins. Every other read, and all writes and commands, still go through the classifier and still ask. It is a default for auto-mode Claude seats, applied at launch: a running seat takes it at its next start. A seat opts out by declaring its own permission options (--permission-mode or --dangerously-skip-permissions), which stay authoritative and get nothing added. Bypass seats are unchanged. Auto is still not a security boundary.

manual.detail: None. A running auto-mode Claude seat takes the rules at its next start.

recovery.detail: Reverting restores the prompt for reads outside the workspace.
